objects.description: Small POD-style class holding checksum data: a 32-bit CRC (ulCRC) and a 16-byte MD5 digest (mD5). Used to represent resource meta/file checksums returned by the module manager interfaces.

Abstract interface for Lua dynamic modules (pre-1.0/DP2.3). Provides logging utilities, function registration into a Lua state, and accessors for resource names and checksums. All methods are pure virtual; the engine supplies an implementation.

Extended interface for modules targeting MTA 1.0. Inherits ILuaModuleManager and adds versioning queries, OS name, resource lookup by name, and ABI-stable resource name/path retrieval using caller-provided buffers.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::ErrorPrintf
functions.description: Prints or logs an error message using a printf-style format string. Intended for reporting module errors to the host (MTA) error channel.
requirements: szFormat must be a valid, null-terminated format string.
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in szFormat (printf-style).
Do not pass nullptr for szFormat.
Thread-safety or reentrancy is unknown; call from contexts permitted by the host.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::DebugPrintf
functions.signature: virtual void DebugPrintf(lua_State* luaVM, const char* szFormat, ...) = 0;
functions.description: Emits a debug message associated with a specific Lua VM using a printf-style format string. Used for module debugging output tied to a particular resource/VM.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State managed by the host.
szFormat must be a valid, null-terminated format string.
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in szFormat (printf-style).
Do not pass nullptr for luaVM or szFormat.
Output destination and formatting follow the host’s debug facilities; thread-safety unknown.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::Printf
functions.description: Prints a general informational message using a printf-style format string. Intended for standard module log/output (non-error, non-debug).
requirements: szFormat must be a valid, null-terminated format string.
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in szFormat (printf-style).
Do not pass nullptr for szFormat.
Output destination is controlled by the host; thread-safety unknown.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::RegisterFunction
functions.signature: virtual bool RegisterFunction(lua_State* luaVM, const char* szFunctionName, lua_CFunction Func) = 0;
functions.description: Registers a C function with the given name into the specified Lua VM, making it callable from Lua scripts.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State for the target resource.
szFunctionName must be a valid, null-terminated string naming the Lua global or function being registered.
Func must be a valid lua_CFunction pointer; do not pass nullptr.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value.
Name collisions, namespace, and registration scope follow host conventions (exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::GetResourceName
functions.signature: virtual bool GetResourceName(lua_State* luaVM, std::string& strName) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the resource name associated with the given Lua VM and writes it into a C++ std::string. Note: May not work if the module and MTA were compiled with different compiler versions.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State associated with a resource.
strName must be a valid reference; the function will assign to it.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value.
Be aware of potential ABI incompatibility between different compiler versions affecting this overload (as noted in the header).

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::GetResourceMetaChecksum
functions.description: Computes/returns the checksum (CRC and MD5) of the meta definition for the resource owning the given Lua VM. Useful for integrity or version checks.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State associated with a resource.
Caller should use the returned CChecksum fields (ulCRC and mD5[16]); endianness/format specifics are not documented.
Behavior on invalid luaVM is unspecified; ensure a valid VM.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager::GetResourceFileChecksum
functions.signature: virtual CChecksum GetResourceFileChecksum(lua_State* luaVM, const char* szFile) = 0;
functions.description: Computes/returns the checksum (CRC and MD5) of a file within the resource associated with the given Lua VM.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State associated with a resource.
szFile must be a valid, null-terminated path/name referring to a resource file; do not pass nullptr.
Path resolution (absolute vs. resource-relative) follows host conventions (unspecified here).
Caller consumes the returned CChecksum (ulCRC and mD5[16]).

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetVersion
functions.description: Returns the host/module manager version as a numeric value. Typically used for compatibility checks.
requirements: No arguments; returned value format/semantics beyond being a version number are unspecified.
Caller should not assume a particular encoding beyond an unsigned long.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetVersionString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable version string of the host/module manager.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as read-only; do not free or modify.
Pointer validity lifetime is managed by the host; copy if long-term storage is needed.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetVersionName
functions.description: Returns a human-readable version name (e.g., release codename) of the host/module manager.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as read-only; do not free or modify.
Pointer lifetime is managed by the host; copy if needed for long-term use.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetNetcodeVersion
functions.description: Returns the network protocol version used by the host. Useful for ensuring network compatibility.
requirements: No arguments; interpretation of the numeric value is host-defined.
Caller should compare against known expected versions for compatibility checks.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetOperatingSystemName
functions.description: Returns the name of the current operating system as a string.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as read-only; do not free or modify.
Pointer lifetime is managed by the host; copy if needed for long-term storage.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetResourceFromName
functions.description: Looks up a resource by name and returns its associated Lua state.
requirements: szResourceName must be a valid, null-terminated resource name string; do not pass nullptr.
Returns a lua_State* on success, or possibly nullptr on failure (behavior not explicitly documented); caller should check for a null result before use.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetResourceName
functions.signature: virtual bool GetResourceName(lua_State* luaVM, char* szName, size_t length) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the resource name associated with the given Lua VM and writes it into a caller-provided C string buffer. This overload avoids the ABI issues of the std::string variant.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State associated with a resource.
szName must be a valid, writable buffer; do not pass nullptr.
length must specify the total size of szName in bytes and be greater than 0.
The buffer must be large enough to hold the name plus a null terminator; if insufficient, the function may fail and return false (exact truncation behavior unspecified).
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: ILuaModuleManager10::GetResourceFilePath
functions.signature: virtual bool GetResourceFilePath(lua_State* luaVM, const char* fileName, char* path, size_t length) = 0;
functions.description: Resolves a file name within the given resource to a full/normalized path and writes it into a caller-provided buffer.
requirements: luaVM must point to a valid lua_State associated with a resource.
fileName must be a valid, null-terminated string naming a file in the resource; do not pass nullptr.
path must be a valid, writable buffer; do not pass nullptr.
length must specify the total size of path in bytes and be greater than 0.
The path buffer must be large enough to hold the resulting path including the null terminator; if not, the function may fail and return false (exact truncation behavior unspecified).
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value.

A general-purpose text string with no specific format constraints. May be empty or contain any bytes; typically used as user-visible text or generic payload.
A Lua/MTA resource identifier string. Expected to be a non-empty, human-readable name consisting of typical filename/identifier characters. Used to look up a resource’s lua_State.
A valid Lua global/function name string. Typically non-empty, composed of letters, digits, and underscores, and often limited in length (e.g., <=64 chars) for registration into a Lua state.
A file name or relative path component string referencing a file within a resource. Usually non-empty, may include path separators, and should be valid under the host’s filesystem rules.
A human-readable version string such as 1.2.3 or similar semantic versions; arbitrary text allowed.
A human-readable version/codename label, e.g., ReleaseCandidate or FuzzEdition; arbitrary text allowed.
A human-readable operating system name string such as Windows, Linux, or UnknownOS.

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: printf format strings and general strings consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# The fuzzer stubs use fixed format strings internally, so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values
# are used strictly as %s arguments and as resource names. We should therefore
# generate:
# - Reasonable ASCII/UTF-8 strings (including empty and long boundary cases)
# - Resource-like names (alnum, underscore, dash) with varied lengths
# - Strings containing spaces and punctuation to exercise logging output
#
# The buffers produced here are intended to seed the fuzzer's random pool so that
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls interesting but valid values.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLES = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
RES_NAME_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-"


def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> int:
    return r.randrange(n)


def _make_resource_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Resource names used by GetResourceFromName; prefer valid, filesystem-safe tokens
    # Mix in variants: simple, namespaced-like, with dashes/underscores, with digits
    styles = ["simple", "ns", "dash", "under", "mixed", "numeric", "long"]

    style = r.choice(styles)
    if style == "simple":
        base = ''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)))
        return base
    if style == "ns":
        a = ''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
        b = ''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
        return f"{a}:{b}"
    if style == "dash":
        parts = [''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4))]
        return '-'.join(parts)
    if style == "under":
        parts = [''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4))]
        return '_'.join(parts)
    if style == "mixed":
        base = ''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
        suf = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)))
        return base + suf
    if style == "numeric":
        return 'res' + ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)))
    if style == "long":
        ln = r.randint(12, 48)
        return ''.join(r.choice(RES_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(ln))
    return "res"


def _make_log_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Strings to be used as %s arguments in Printf/ErrorPrintf/DebugPrintf
    variants = []
    # Empty and small
    variants.append("")
    variants.append("a")
    variants.append("ok")
    variants.append("hello")
    # Whitespace-heavy
    variants.append("   ")
    variants.append("\tindented\nline")
    # Punctuation and format-like content (but safe as plain string)
    variants.append("value=%d; ptr=%p; str=%s")
    variants.append("{\"k\":\"v\",\"n\":123}")
    variants.append("[INFO] ready")
    variants.append("path/to/file.lua")
    # Unicode (valid UTF-8)
    variants.append("naïve café ☕")
    variants.append("日本語リソース")
    # Long-ish
    long1 = ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLES) for _ in range(r.randint(32, 96)))
    variants.append(long1)
    # Alnum
    variants.append(''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 32))))

    # Random constructed
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        ln = r.randint(1, 128)
        s = ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLES) for _ in range(ln))
        variants.append(s)

    return r.choice(variants)


def _encode_cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode UTF-8 with a single trailing NUL for C strings
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b'\x00'


def _pick(entries: List[bytes], r: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[bytes]:
    # Pick a subset that fits within budget
    out = []
    r.shuffle(entries)
    total = 0
    for e in entries:
        if total + len(e) <= budget:
            out.append(e)
            total += len(e)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # We generate a set of C-strings concatenated together, since the harness
    # typically reads from its input stream to populate multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls.
    # Each string is NUL-terminated to allow robust tokenization by the fuzz shim.

    # Construct a balanced corpus:
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure at least one valid resource name (non-empty) for DebugPrintf path
    res = _make_resource_name(r)
    if not res:
        res = "res"
    entries.append(_encode_cstr(res))

    # Add additional candidate resource names to explore different lookups
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        entries.append(_encode_cstr(_make_resource_name(r)))

    # Add log strings for %s arguments
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        entries.append(_encode_cstr(_make_log_string(r)))

    # Boundary cases: empty, very long printable, and path-like names
    entries.append(_encode_cstr(""))
    long_printable = ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLES) for _ in range(r.randint(128, 512)))
    entries.append(_encode_cstr(long_printable))
    entries.append(_encode_cstr("res-with-dash_underscore123"))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order lightly
    seen = set()
    deduped: List[bytes] = []
    for e in entries:
        if e not in seen:
            seen.add(e)
            deduped.append(e)

    # Respect overall size limit
    payloads = _pick(deduped, r, MAX_TOTAL)

    # Concatenate; keep as a pure byte stream of NUL-terminated strings
    data = b''.join(payloads)

    # Safety: cap to MAX_TOTAL
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzz stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - resource names (used to look up a lua_State via GetResourceFromName)
# - general printf string arguments
# and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME is not used in provided stubs.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a single bytes buffer that encodes one or more newline-separated strings.
# - The first string will be a plausible resource name (alnum/underscore/dash), non-empty,
#   to maximize chances GetResourceFromName succeeds.
# - Follow with several additional strings containing a wide variety of content to exercise
#   printf formatting paths: ASCII words, numbers, long strings, Unicode, percent signs,
#   null-byte-including segments encoded via length-prefix to allow the harness to read up
#   to a newline while still containing rich content before it (we avoid actual NULs since
#   fuzzer expects C strings).
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: The fuzz harness typically pulls a string per FUZZ_PARAM_STR call in order of usage.
#       We'll provide multiple lines so each call can consume the next line.

SAFE_RESOURCE_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-"

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "hello", "world", "test", "module", "resource", "alpha", "beta", "gamma",
    "delta", "printf", "debug", "error", "info", "lua", "state", "checksum",
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "✓", "😀", "Привет", "こんにちは", "안녕하세요", "مرحبا", "हैलो", "שלום", "ñandú", "résumé",
]

EDGE_PATTERNS = [
    "%", "%%", "%s", "%d", "%p", "%08X", "%lld", "%u", "{0}", "${VAR}",
    "\\n", "\\r\\n", "\t", " ", "\u0000",  # Note: actual NUL avoided; literal sequence only
]

NUMBERS = ["0", "1", "-1", "42", "1337", "2147483647", "-2147483648", "4294967295"]


def _rand_res_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Length between 1 and 32
    length = rnd.randint(3, 16)
    # Ensure starts with alpha to resemble typical resource names
    start = rnd.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")
    rest = "".join(rnd.choice(SAFE_RESOURCE_CHARS) for _ in range(length - 1))
    # Occasionally include a dash or underscore separated pattern
    if length > 6 and rnd.random() < 0.4:
        pivot = rnd.randint(2, length - 2)
        rest = rest[:pivot] + rnd.choice(["-", "_"]) + rest[pivot:]
    return start + rest


def _rand_ascii_blob(rnd: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    pool = ASCII_WORDS + NUMBERS + EDGE_PATTERNS
    parts: List[str] = []
    while sum(len(p) + 1 for p in parts) < target_len:
        parts.append(rnd.choice(pool))
    s = " ".join(parts)
    return s[:target_len]


def _rand_unicode_blob(rnd: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with Unicode to form a valid UTF-8 string
    parts: List[str] = []
    while len("".join(parts).encode("utf-8")) < target_len:
        parts.append(rnd.choice(ASCII_WORDS + ["-", "_", "/"]))
        parts.append(rnd.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # trim to target_len bytes when UTF-8 encoded without breaking encoding
    b = s.encode("utf-8")[:target_len]
    # ensure valid utf-8 by backing off to a complete sequence
    while True:
        try:
            return b.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
            b = b[:e.start]
            if not b:
                return ""


def _lines_for_run(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # 1) Resource name for DebugPrintf GetResourceFromName
    lines.append(_rand_res_name(rnd))

    # 2) General string for ErrorPrintf/Printf first %s
    # Keep moderate size
    lines.append(_rand_ascii_blob(rnd, rnd.randint(8, 64)))

    # 3) Another string for DebugPrintf %s with mix of unicode and format-like tokens
    lines.append(_rand_unicode_blob(rnd, rnd.randint(16, 96)))

    # 4) Very short string (edge case)
    lines.append(rnd.choice(["a", "0", "-", "%"]))

    # 5) Longer path-like or name-like string
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # path-like
        segs = [_rand_res_name(rnd) for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4))]
        lines.append("/".join(segs))
    else:
        lines.append(_rand_ascii_blob(rnd, rnd.randint(32, 128)))

    # 6) Percent-heavy string to test escaping but still valid as data argument
    percenty = "".join(rnd.choice(["%", "%%", "x", "s", "d"]) for _ in range(rnd.randint(10, 40)))
    lines.append(percenty)

    # 7) Very long but bounded UTF-8 content (ensure overall buffer <= 4096)
    lines.append(_rand_unicode_blob(rnd, rnd.randint(128, 512)))

    return lines


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose multiple scenarios in one buffer occasionally to feed more FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    scenario_count = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.6 else rnd.randint(2, 4)

    all_lines: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(scenario_count):
        all_lines.extend(_lines_for_run(rnd))

    # Join with newlines; avoid embedded NULs since consumer expects C strings
    blob = "\n".join(all_lines)

    # Ensure size limit
    max_bytes = 4096
    data = blob.encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        data = data[:max_bytes]
        # Trim to avoid cutting a multi-byte sequence
        while True:
            try:
                data.decode("utf-8")
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
                data = data[:e.start]
                if not data:
                    break
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid input buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# used by the ILuaModuleManager10-focused fuzzers. The stubs primarily request:
# - Resource names (non-empty, <= ~64 chars)
# - Filenames within a resource (e.g., meta.xml or other plausible names)
# - Version strings/names/OS names
# - Assorted other strings for printf/debug and registration names
#
# The harness is likely to parse the provided bytes into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls sequentially. We therefore emit a sequence of newline-separated strings
# followed by some 32-bit integers for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls.
#
# Format strategy (line-oriented):
# - Provide 1..3 resource names following pattern: <base>_<index>
# - Then provide several generic strings for use in various stubs (func names, filenames, etc.)
# - Include plausible filenames like meta.xml, script.lua, data/config.json, images/tex.png
# - Keep each line non-empty and within reasonable size limits the stubs expect
# - Append a small tail of binary 32-bit little-endian unsigned ints to satisfy integer params
#
# The output stays under 4096 bytes and is deterministic for a given seed.

IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
FILENAME_CHARS = IDENT_CHARS + "/._"

def _rand_ident(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rnd.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(max(1, n)))
    # avoid starting with digit to be more name-like
    if s and s[0].isdigit():
        s = 'r' + s[1:]
    return s

def _rand_filename(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weighted choices of common resource files
    choices = [
        "meta.xml",
        "script.lua",
        "client.lua",
        "server.lua",
        "config.xml",
        "data/config.json",
        "data/table.csv",
        "images/tex.png",
        "models/veh.dff",
        "models/veh.txd",
        "docs/readme.txt",
    ]
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        return rnd.choice(choices)
    # Otherwise synthesize a plausible path
    parts = []
    depth = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else rnd.randint(2, 3)
    for _ in range(depth - 1):
        parts.append(_rand_ident(rnd, 3, 10).lower())
    base = _rand_ident(rnd, 3, 12).lower()
    ext = rnd.choice([".xml", ".lua", ".json", ".txt", ".png", ".dff", ".txd", ".cfg"]) 
    parts.append(base + ext)
    return '/'.join(parts)

def _bounded(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    if len(s) <= max_len:
        return s
    return s[:max_len]

def _make_resource_names(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    count = rnd.randint(1, 3)
    base = _rand_ident(rnd, 3, 12)
    base = _bounded(base, 32)
    names = [f"{base}_{i}" for i in range(count)]
    return names

def _version_string(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    major = rnd.randint(0, 10)
    minor = rnd.randint(0, 20)
    patch = rnd.randint(0, 50)
    suffix = rnd.choice(["", "-dev", "-rc1", "-beta", "-fuzz"]) 
    return _bounded(f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}{suffix}", 64)

def _version_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    codenames = [
        "FuzzEdition", "Aurora", "Beacon", "Catalyst", "Delta",
        "Echo", "Falcon", "Genesis", "Helix", "Ion",
    ]
    return _bounded(rnd.choice(codenames), 64)

def _os_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return _bounded(rnd.choice([
        "Windows", "Linux", "macOS", "FreeBSD", "UnknownOS"
    ]), 64)

def _func_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Lua global function-style name
    base = _rand_ident(rnd, 1, 12)
    return _bounded(base, 63)

def _random_misc_string(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # For general DebugPrintf argument s, etc.
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return _bounded(_rand_ident(rnd, 1, 24), 64)
    # Include some punctuation sometimes
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .,:/"
    n = rnd.randint(1, 48)
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))

def _u32_le(n: int) -> bytes:
    n &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    lines: List[str] = []

    # 1) Construct 1..3 resource names used by the manager factory
    res_names = _make_resource_names(rnd)
    lines.extend(res_names)

    # 2) Version metadata strings for manager factory
    lines.append(_version_string(rnd))        # verStr
    lines.append(_version_name(rnd))          # verName
    lines.append(_os_name(rnd))               # osName

    # 3) Additional resource query names used by stubs; include exact and partial names
    lines.append(res_names[0])                # direct hit
    # Partial or variant to exercise substring matching in GetResourceFromName
    partial = res_names[0][: max(1, min(len(res_names[0]), rnd.randint(1, 5)))]
    lines.append(partial)

    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):

    # 5) Filenames for file checksum and path resolution
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4)):

    # 6) Misc strings for DebugPrintf message arguments or other generic uses
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 5)):
        lines.append(_random_misc_string(rnd))

    # Ensure none are empty; replace empties with defaults
    cleaned = []
    for s in lines:
        if not s:
            s = "res"
        # Avoid leading/trailing whitespace that might be trimmed unexpectedly
        s = s.strip()
        if not s:
            s = "res"
        cleaned.append(s)

    text_payload = ("\n".join(cleaned) + "\n").encode('utf-8')

    # 7) Append several unsigned ints for stubs that pull FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    # Provide values that cover interesting cases
    ints: List[int] = []
    # Generic randoms
    for _ in range(4):
        ints.append(rnd.getrandbits(32))
    # Boundary-biased integers for buffer sizing in stubs (mod 256/512 usage)
    ints += [0, 1, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1024, 0xFFFFFFFF]

    int_payload = b''.join(_u32_le(x) for x in ints)

    out = text_payload + int_payload
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid strings for two FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses in the stub:
# 1) Resource name for ILuaModuleManager10::GetResourceFromName
# 2) Lua identifier for ILuaModuleManager::RegisterFunction
#
# Goals:
# - Provide plausible resource names (alphanumeric, underscore, dashes) with some
#   common prefixes/suffixes to exercise lookup variations.
# - Provide valid Lua identifiers (start with letter or underscore, followed by letters/digits/underscores),
#   non-empty, length <= 63 per stub logic.
# - Pack both strings into a single buffer that the fuzzer framework can split/consume
#   as separate FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We separate with newlines. If the framework
#   reads sequentially, it will take first line as resName and second line as funcName.
#
# The output is a bytes payload with: b"<resName>\n<funcName>\n"

RES_PREFIXES: List[str] = [
    "res", "resource", "mod", "pkg", "lib", "game", "map", "ui", "net", "snd",
]
RES_SUFFIXES: List[str] = [
    "", "_v1", "_v2", "-test", "-dev", "_debug", "_release", "-alpha", "-beta", "_lite",
]

LUA_FIRST_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + "_"
LUA_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

RES_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"

MAX_FUNC_LEN = 63  # stub trims to 63

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _rand_res_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose resource names like: prefix + optional number + optional separator + core + suffix
    prefix = r.choice(RES_PREFIXES)
    core_len = r.randint(1, 12)
    core = ''.join(r.choice(RES_CHARS) for _ in range(core_len))
    sep = r.choice(['', '-', '_'])
    suffix = r.choice(RES_SUFFIXES)
    maybe_num = str(r.randint(1, 999)) if _rand_bool(r, 0.4) else ''
    parts = [prefix]
    if maybe_num:
        parts.append(maybe_num)
    if sep:
        parts.append(sep)
    parts.append(core)
    final = ''.join(parts) + suffix
    # Ensure non-empty and reasonable length
    if not final:
        final = 'res'
    return final[:128]

def _rand_lua_identifier(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Start char must be letter or underscore
    first = r.choice(LUA_FIRST_CHARS)
    # Choose length 1..63 (inclusive)
    remaining_len = r.randint(0, MAX_FUNC_LEN - 1)
    rest = ''.join(r.choice(LUA_CHARS) for _ in range(remaining_len))
    ident = first + rest
    # Bias towards some interesting names
    specials = [
        'f', 'init', 'update', 'onStart', 'on_stop', 'handleEvent', 'process',
        '_', '_G', 'main', 'tick', 'Render', 'NetHandler', 'CRC32', 'MD5',
    ]
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.15):
        ident = r.choice(specials)
    # Enforce max length
    return ident[:MAX_FUNC_LEN]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a mix: sometimes short canonical names, sometimes longer/randomized
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        res_name = 'res'
    else:
        res_name = _rand_res_name(r)

    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        func_name = 'f'
    else:
        func_name = _rand_lua_identifier(r)

    # Assemble payload as two lines to feed sequential FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    payload = f"{res_name}\n{func_name}\n"
    return payload.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(items)

def _weighted_bool(rng: random.Random, p_true: float) -> bool:
    return rng.random() < p_true

RESOURCE_NAMES_COMMON = [
    "res", "admin", "default", "core", "gameplay", "map", "test", "utils",
    "vehicles", "weapons", "skins", "gui", "hud", "audio", "net", "fs",
]

FILE_NAMES_COMMON = [
    "meta.xml",
    "script.lua",
    "client.lua",

    "sounds/music.ogg",
]

# Generate a plausible resource name (letters, digits, underscore, dash)
def _gen_resource_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.5):
        return _rand_choice(rng, RESOURCE_NAMES_COMMON)
    length = rng.randint(3, 24)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    # Avoid starting with dash for typical name rules
    first_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    s = rng.choice(first_chars)
    s += "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return s

# Generate a plausible resource-relative filename/path
def _gen_resource_file(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.55):
        base = _rand_choice(rng, FILE_NAMES_COMMON)
    else:
        # Build a custom path: optional one or two directories, then a filename with extension
        dirs = []
        if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.8):
            n_dirs = 1 if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.7) else 2
            for _ in range(n_dirs):
                dlen = rng.randint(2, 12)
                dirs.append("".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(dlen)))
        fname_len = rng.randint(3, 16)
        fname = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(fname_len))
        ext = _rand_choice(rng, [".lua", ".xml", ".json", ".txt", ".png", ".dds", ".wav", ".ogg", ".cfg"]) if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.9) else ""
        base = "/".join(dirs + [fname + ext]) if dirs else (fname + ext)
    # Ensure length constraints as per stubs (<= 128 and <= 96 in places). We'll stay well below.
    if len(base) > 96:
        base = base[:96]
    if not base:
        base = "meta.xml"
    return base

# Encode as two null-terminated strings concatenated: resourceName\0fileName\0
# This aligns well with FUZZ_PARAM_STR extractions that may split the input.
# The fuzzing harness typically pulls independent strings, but providing both
# in one buffer helps seed both FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls with meaningful values.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    res_name = _gen_resource_name(rng)
    file_name = _gen_resource_file(rng)

    # Occasionally produce longer paths or tricky names to explore behavior
    if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.2):
        # Add relative elements but keep valid (no traversal outside resource)
        # Avoid leading slash; include single "." segments sometimes
        prefixes = []
        if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.5):
            prefixes.append(".")
        if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.3):
            prefixes.append("assets")
        extra = "/".join(prefixes + [file_name]) if prefixes else file_name
        file_name = extra[:120] if len(extra) > 120 else extra

    # Construct buffer: resName\0fileName\0 and pad with a small random trailer to vary seeds
    parts = [res_name.encode("utf-8"), b"\x00", file_name.encode("utf-8"), b"\x00"]

    # Small, valid trailer comprised of additional candidate names separated by NULs
    if _weighted_bool(rng, 0.3):
        # Add a couple more plausible filenames as optional extras
        extras = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            extras.append(_gen_resource_file(rng).encode("utf-8"))
        for e in extras:
            parts.append(e)
            parts.append(b"\x00")

    data = b"".join(parts)

    # Enforce maximum size
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: "version string" used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the stub to populate:
# - verStr (GetVersionString)
# - verName (GetVersionName)
# - osName (GetOperatingSystemName)
# Plus additional arbitrary strings for resource base names.
# The stub limits strings to certain lengths (64 for version/name/os, 32 for resource base),
# and synthesizes resource names as base + "_" + index. It also creates 1..3 resources.
# It also pulls two unsigned ints for version/net numbers and a third for resource count modulo 3.
#
# Our goal is to provide a single byte buffer that FUZZ framework will slice into for
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls, yielding valid and interesting values.
#
# Assumptions about FUZZ framework (typical patterns):
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads a length-prefixed or NUL-terminated slice from input. To stay broadly
#   compatible, we encode our buffer as a sequence of NUL-terminated strings followed by a
#   series of 32-bit little-endian integers. Many frameworks consume in call order.
# - Even if exact mechanics differ, providing clear NUL-terminated strings and aligned integers
#   tends to produce stable, valid values in common harnesses.
#
# We therefore build the buffer in the exact order of consumption in the stub:
#   1) verStr  (string, <=64)
#   2) verName (string, <=64)
#   3) osName  (string, <=64)
#   4) verNum  (uint32)
#   5) netNum  (uint32)
#   6) countSeed (uint32) -> determines resource count 1..3 via %3 + 1
#   7) For i in [0..count-1]: base string (<=32). Stub appends _i.
#
# We pick values to exercise different behaviors:
# - Version strings: semantic, long with metadata, unusual characters but printable, and edge lengths.
# - Version name: codename-like strings, include spaces and dashes.
# - OS name: common OS identifiers and exotic names.
# - Numbers: choose varied ranges to impact checksum generation and internal state.
# - Resource bases: mix short, max-length, with dashes/periods and unicode-like ASCII approximations.
#
# The generator stays under 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SEMVER_CORES = [
    "1.0.0", "2.3.4", "0.9.9", "10.0.1", "2024.1.0", "3.0.0", "1.2.3",
]
PRE_RELEASE_IDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "rc.1", "rc.2", "dev", "exp", "nightly", "preview",
]
BUILD_META_IDS = [
    "001", "build.123", "gabcdef", "sha.012345", "win", "linux", "x64", "arm64",
]
CODENAMES = [
    "FuzzEdition", "Long Term Support", "Dragon-Edge", "Blue Sky", "Neon",
    "Zebra", "Falcon-Prime", "Omega", "Aurora", "Quantum",
]
OSNAMES = [
    "Windows", "Windows_NT", "Linux", "GNU/Linux", "macOS", "FreeBSD",
    "OpenBSD", "NetBSD", "Solaris", "UnknownOS", "Haiku",
]
RES_BASES = [
    "res", "core", "assets", "textures", "scripts", "audio", "ui", "data",
    "pkg", "module", "resource", "checksum", "mtasa", "lua",
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .-_+:/"


def rand_semver(r: random.Random) -> str:
    core = r.choice(SEMVER_CORES)
    parts = [core]
    # Optionally add pre-release
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        pre_count = 1 if r.random() < 0.7 else 2
        pres = [r.choice(PRE_RELEASE_IDS) for _ in range(pre_count)]
        parts.append("-" + ".".join(pres))
    # Optionally add build metadata
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        bcount = 1 if r.random() < 0.7 else 2
        metas = [r.choice(BUILD_META_IDS) for _ in range(bcount)]
        parts.append("+" + ".".join(metas))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Ensure <=64 as per stub truncation preference
    return s[:64]


def rand_codename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(CODENAMES)
    # Optionally add minor versioning tag or year
    suffixes = [
        "", " R" + str(r.randint(1, 5)),
        " Update " + str(r.randint(1, 4)),
        " " + str(r.randint(2000, 2035)),
    ]
    name = base + r.choice(suffixes)
    # Mix spacing or dashes
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        name = name.replace(" ", "-")
    return name[:64]


def rand_osname(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        name = r.choice(OSNAMES)
    else:
        # Compose custom OS string
        vendor = r.choice(["ContosoOS", "FuzzOS", "ProtoOS", "EdgeOS", "MegaOS"])
        ver = rand_semver(r)
        name = f"{vendor} {ver}"
    return name[:64]


def rand_uint32(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose from interesting value sets including boundaries and randoms
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
               1023, 1024, 4095, 4096, 2**32 - 1]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(choices)
    # Otherwise return fully random 32-bit value
    return r.getrandbits(32)


def rand_base_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = r.choice(RES_BASES)
    else:
        # Build a safe random token 3..16 chars
        n = r.randint(3, 16)
        base = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
        if not base:
            base = "res"
    # Add optional sub-qualifier
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tag = r.choice(["dev", "rc", "hd", "lo", "common", "shared"]) if r.random() < 0.7 else str(r.randint(1, 9999))
        sep = r.choice(["-", ".", "_"])
        base = f"{base}{sep}{tag}"
    return base[:32] if base else "res"


def put_cstr(buf: bytearray, s: str):
    # Ensure NUL-terminated C string using UTF-8-safe ASCII. Stub doesn't require UTF-8 but safe.
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Avoid embedded NULs
    data = data.replace(b"\x00", b"?")
    buf.extend(data)
    buf.append(0)


def put_u32le(buf: bytearray, v: int):
    v &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    buf.extend(bytes((v & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, (v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 24) & 0xFF)))


def build_buffer(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    buf = bytearray()

    # 1) verStr
    ver_str = rand_semver(r)
    put_cstr(buf, ver_str)

    # 2) verName
    ver_name = rand_codename(r)
    put_cstr(buf, ver_name)

    # 3) osName
    os_name = rand_osname(r)
    put_cstr(buf, os_name)

    # 4) verNum
    ver_num = rand_uint32(r)
    put_u32le(buf, ver_num)

    # 5) netNum
    net_num = rand_uint32(r)
    put_u32le(buf, net_num)

    # 6) countSeed
    # Choose seed to exercise 1..3 resources evenly
    count = r.randint(1, 3)
    # Find a seed such that (seed % 3) + 1 == count
    rem = (count - 1) % 3
    # Create a seed with desired remainder but also varied magnitude
    base = rand_uint32(r) & ~0x3
    seed = base | rem
    put_u32le(buf, seed)

    # 7) Resource base strings
    for _ in range(count):
        base_name = rand_base_name(r)
        put_cstr(buf, base_name)

    # Safety cap
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return build_buffer(r)

import random
import struct
import hashlib
from typing import List

# Target data type: "version name" (human-readable version/codename label)
# The fuzzer stub consumes several FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values used as:
#   - verStr (version string)
#   - verName (version name/codename)
#   - osName (operating system name)
#   - base (resource base names), 1..3 resources
# It also consumes a few FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) values for version numbers and count.
#
# Our job: emit a single bytes buffer that the harness will split into FUZZ_PARAM_* pieces.
# We therefore pack multiple strings and integers in a deterministic, self-describing way.
#
# Design of buffer format (compact, valid, and diverse):
#   - Header magic: b"LMGR10\0"
#   - verNum (u32 LE)
#   - netNum (u32 LE)
#   - count (u32 LE) in range 1..3
#   - verStr (len-prefixed UTF-8, 1..64 bytes)
#   - verName (1..64)
#   - osName (1..64)
#   - For each resource i in [0..count-1]: baseName (1..32)
#
# Values are chosen from curated sets and randomized with the given seed to provide
# valid but varied inputs. All strings are ASCII/UTF-8 without nulls and within the
# size constraints the stub enforces (it truncates if longer, but we keep them within limits).

OS_NAMES = [
    "Windows", "Linux", "macOS", "FreeBSD", "OpenBSD", "NetBSD", "Solaris", "Haiku",
    "Android", "iOS", "UnknownOS"
]

VER_PREFIX = [
    "0.1", "0.9", "1.0", "1.1", "1.2", "2.0", "3.5", "10.0", "2024.1", "2025.7"
]

VER_TAGS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "rc1", "rc2", "stable", "LTS", "preview", "nightly", "exp", "hotfix"
]

CODENAMES = [
    "FuzzEdition", "Thunderbolt", "Nebula", "Quasar", "Aurora", "Zenith", "Nimbus",
    "Eclipse", "Odyssey", "Pioneer", "Voyager", "Atlas"
]

RES_BASE_WORDS = [
    "core", "ui", "net", "audio", "physics", "render", "entity", "world", "vehicle", "ped",
    "mission", "map", "hud", "input", "anim", "camera"
]

# Utility: build a version string that looks realistic and stays <= 64 chars

def build_version_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose like: <prefix>.<patch>[-<tag>][-build<nnn>]
    prefix = r.choice(VER_PREFIX)
    patch = r.randint(0, 15)
    s = f"{prefix}.{patch}"
    # Optional tag
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        s += f"-{r.choice(VER_TAGS)}"
    # Optional build metadata
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        s += f"+build{r.randint(1, 9999)}"
    # Ensure <= 64
    return s[:64]

# Utility: build a version codename <= 64

def build_version_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Either a single codename or codename with cycle/year
    name = r.choice(CODENAMES)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        # Add cycle or year
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            name += f"-{r.randint(1, 12)}"
        else:
            name += f"-{r.randint(2008, 2035)}"
    return name[:64]

# Utility: build OS name <= 64

def build_os_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(OS_NAMES)
    if base in ("Windows", "Linux", "FreeBSD", "OpenBSD", "NetBSD") and r.random() < 0.7:
        # Add variant/version
        tail = r.choice([
            "XP", "7", "8.1", "10", "11", "Server", "Mint", "Arch", "Debian",
            "Ubuntu", "Fedora", "22.04", "24.04", "13.2", "CURRENT"
        ])
        return f"{base} {tail}"[:64]
    if base == "macOS" and r.random() < 0.7:
        tail = r.choice(["Monterey", "Ventura", "Sonoma", "Sequoia"]) 
        return f"{base} {tail}"[:64]
    return base

# Utility: resource base names 1..32 chars, ASCII

def build_res_base(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose 1-2 words and optional suffix
    parts = [r.choice(RES_BASE_WORDS)]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(r.choice(RES_BASE_WORDS))
    base = "_".join(parts)
    # Optional variant
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            base += f"_{r.randint(0, 9)}"
        else:
            base += f"_{r.choice(['dbg','opt','hi','lo','hd','sd'])}"
    # Ensure length bounds
    if len(base) < 1:
        base = "res"
    return base[:32]

# Helper to encode a length-prefixed UTF-8 string with 1..max_len length

def put_lp_string(buf: bytearray, s: str, max_len: int) -> None:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) == 0:
        b = b"a"
    if len(b) > max_len:
        b = b[:max_len]
    buf += struct.pack('<H', len(b))
    buf += b

# Generate deterministic but varied unsigned long values; keep them wide-ranging

def pick_version_numbers(r: random.Random):
    # Create two 32-bit values with some structure
    # verNum encodes major/minor/patch in bytes
    major = r.randint(0, 255)
    minor = r.randint(0, 255)
    patch = r.randint(0, 255)
    extra = r.randint(0, 255)
    verNum = (extra << 24) | (major << 16) | (minor << 8) | patch

    # netNum uses a hash of string components for determinism variety
    seed_str = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{extra}".encode()
    h = hashlib.blake2s(seed_str, digest_size=4).digest()
    netNum = struct.unpack('<I', h)[0]
    return verNum, netNum

# Main entry

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    buf = bytearray()

    # Magic header to help triage inputs
    buf += b"LMGR10\x00"

    verNum, netNum = pick_version_numbers(r)
    count = r.randint(1, 3)

    buf += struct.pack('<I', verNum)
    buf += struct.pack('<I', netNum)
    buf += struct.pack('<I', count)

    verStr = build_version_string(r)
    verName = build_version_name(r)
    osName = build_os_name(r)

    put_lp_string(buf, verStr, 64)
    put_lp_string(buf, verName, 64)
    put_lp_string(buf, osName, 64)

    for _ in range(count):
        base = build_res_base(r)
        put_lp_string(buf, base, 32)

    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes (it will be much smaller)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        return bytes(buf[:4096])
    return bytes(buf)

# This generator targets string buffers consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the FakeLuaModuleManager10 fuzzer stub.
# The stub uses these strings for:
# - Version string (verStr): default "1.0.0", truncated to 64
# - Version name (verName): human-readable codename, truncated to 64
# - OS name (osName): human-readable operating system name, truncated to 64
# - Resource base names (base): up to 32 chars, then suffixed with _<index>
# It also consumes two unsigned ints (verNum/netNum) and one unsigned int for resource count (mod 3 + 1),
# but these come from FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) rather than FUZZ_PARAM_STR and are not directly fed from our bytes.
# Our job is to provide a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice/consume for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We'll encode multiple newline-separated fields so the fuzzer can parse them as distinct strings in order.
# We ensure values are valid, interesting, and exercise different code paths (equality, substring match, truncation, empty defaulting avoidance).

    "Windows",
    "Linux",
    "macOS",
    "FreeBSD",
    "Android",
    "iOS",
    "UnknownOS",
]

VER_PREFIXES = ["0.9.", "1.0.", "1.1.", "2.0.", "2024.", "10."]
VER_SUFFIXES = ["alpha", "beta", "rc1", "rc2", "stable", "LTS"]

CODENAMES = [
    "FuzzEdition",
    "Nightly",
    "Canary",
    "Dragon",
    "Phoenix",
    "Omega",
    "Zeta",
    "Nebula",
]

# Some resource bases meant to trigger exact and substring behaviors in GetResourceFromName
RESOURCE_BASE_SETS = [
    ["core", "coreutils", "utils"],
    ["res", "resmod", "mod"],
    ["game", "gameplay", "play"],
    ["alpha", "alphabet", "beta"],
    ["data", "metadata", "meta"],
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


def _make_version_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate versions like 1.2.3, 2024.1, or 1.0.0-rc1, within 64 chars
    major = rng.randint(0, 20)
    minor = rng.randint(0, 20)
    patch = rng.randint(0, 50)
    style = rng.randrange(4)
    if style == 0:
        ver = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}"
    elif style == 1:
        ver = f"{_rand_choice(rng, VER_PREFIXES)}{rng.randint(0, 99)}"
    elif style == 2:
        ver = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{_rand_choice(rng, VER_SUFFIXES)}"
    else:
        ver = f"v{major}.{minor}"
    # Occasionally hit truncation boundary (64)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(30, 80)))
        ver = (ver + "-" + extra)[:70]  # still safe before stub truncates to 64
    return ver[:64] or "1.0.0"


def _make_version_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_choice(rng, CODENAMES)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += f" {rng.randint(1, 9)}"
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # avoid f-string list literal; pick separately
        stage = _rand_choice(rng, ["dev", "stable", "preview", "lts"])
        base += f" ({stage})"
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # Try to exceed 64 to trigger truncation behavior
        base += "-" + ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(80))
    return base[:64] or "FuzzEdition"


def _make_os_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        name = _rand_choice(rng, OS_NAMES)
    else:
        # Custom OS string
        vendor = _rand_choice(rng, ["Contoso", "Acme", "Umbrella", "Wayne", "Stark"])
        name = f"{vendor}OS {rng.randint(1, 12)}.{rng.randint(0, 9)}"
    # Occasionally push the truncation
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        name += "-" + ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(70))
    return name[:64] or "UnknownOS"


def _make_resource_bases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Pick a set that includes overlapping names to exercise substring matching
    base_set = _rand_choice(rng, RESOURCE_BASE_SETS)
    # Also add a random custom base sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        custom_len = rng.randint(3, 20)
        custom = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(custom_len))
        base_set = list(dict.fromkeys(base_set + [custom]))
    # Enforce 1..3 number of resources; the stub itself picks count from unsigned param,
    # but we provide up to 3 base names so any consumption order has valid data.
    rng.shuffle(base_set)
    base_set = base_set[:3]
    # Ensure each base is non-empty and <=32
    out = []
    for b in base_set:
        b = b.strip().strip("\0")
        if not b:
            b = "res"
        if len(b) > 32:
            b = b[:32]
        out.append(b)
    # Ensure at least one base shares a substring with another to trigger the fallback search
    if len(out) >= 2 and rng.random() < 0.6:
        out[1] = (out[0] + "utils")[:32]
    return out


def _pack_strings(fields: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines, which most FUZZ_PARAM_STR implementations can split by
    blob = "\n".join(fields)
    b = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    return b[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    ver_str = _make_version_string(rng)
    ver_name = _make_version_name(rng)
    os_name = _make_os_name(rng)
    bases = _make_resource_bases(rng)

    # Provide additional filler strings to satisfy any extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls beyond our expected ones
    # and to allow the stub to pull different base values for multiple resources.
    filler = []
    for b in bases:
        # Include raw base and some variants to diversify names used when the stub concatenates _<i>
        filler.append(b)
        if len(b) >= 2:
            filler.append(b[:2])
        filler.append(b + "-alt")

    # First entries should map to verStr, verName, osName usage in the stub.
    fields: List[str] = [ver_str, ver_name, os_name]

    # Then a pool of resource base candidates; the stub will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR per resource.
    fields.extend(bases)

    # Add extra pool strings so future FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls remain valid and non-empty.
    fields.extend(filler)

    # Ensure no empty strings so the stub doesn't replace with defaults unless desired.
    fields = [s if s else "X" for s in fields]

    return _pack_strings(fields)
